analyst_view.overall: Brest (6th, 18 points) host Paris FC (2nd, 23 points) in a top-six meeting after both won last weekend: Brest 1-0 at Strasbourg for a third straight league win and clean sheet, Paris FC 4-0 against Angers after beating Monaco and Auxerre. Brest are without Brendan Chardonnet (calf) and Raphael Le Guen (long-term), Kenny Lala started at Strasbourg but is listed as questionable (the numbers already take him off), and creative midfielder Kamory Doumbia is doubtful with an ankle problem, which the numbers do not know. Liam Rosenior's Paris FC miss Nhoa Sangui (hamstring, counted) and are otherwise expected to field the side that beat Angers; they have the best home record in the league but this is away. Ruddy Buquet referees (confirmed by the club's preview); the numbers use his 3.2 cards a game in their sample and already take about 15% off the cards for him. Fresh previews add nothing big beyond Doumbia's doubt, so the view stays with the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, 1.3 for Brest and 1.5 for Paris FC, and they already count Brest's three clean sheets, Paris FC's 13 goals in six and Lala's absence. Brest have created plenty this season but missed many big chances, and Doumbia's doubtful ankle could blunt them, while Paris FC are short only Sangui at the back; those pull against each other, so I stay at 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners. Brest have won only 13 corners in their last six while Paris FC have won 31, and the numbers already move both sides for that form. Both teams are expected to line up much as last weekend, so nothing changes how either side attacks and I stay at about 9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards, down from about 4 because Ruddy Buquet is the referee (3.2 cards a game in their sample, below the 3.9 average), and they already count Paris FC's 15 cards in their last six. The club preview gives him a higher long-run yellow-card average, but that is his whole career, not news, and there is no rivalry or discipline story, so I stay at 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.0 shots. Brest have been winning without creating much lately, while Paris FC have been shooting more than usual, and both trends are in the numbers' momentum. Doumbia's doubtful ankle could make Brest a little blunter, but he may still play, so I stay at 24.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target. Paris FC have hit the target 35 times in six games and Brest have allowed only 17 in their last six, with goalkeeper Selvik on three straight clean sheets, and the numbers already balance those runs. With nothing big missing that they don't know about, I stay at 8.
